title: Form Engine Docs and OBS Field Rendering

answers.question: Where is the form engine documented, and how does the form engine library implement rendering of obs fields?

paragraphs.text: The form engine is documented in the `openmrs-contrib-o3-docs` repository under "Forms in O3", and the React Form Engine library (`openmrs-esm-form-engine-lib`) implements obs-field rendering as a two-part contract: `type` picks a *value adapter* that reads and writes observation (obs) data, and `questionOptions.rendering` picks the *input control* that is displayed.
## Where the form engine is documented

The canonical guide lives in `content/en-US/docs/forms-in-o3/`. Its overview page states that O3 Forms is the Reference Application's default workflow and names the four moving parts: the Form Builder app, the patient forms app, the `@openmrs/esm-form-engine-app` integration that registers `react-form-engine-widget` into `form-widget-slot`, and `@openmrs/esm-form-engine-lib` which provides the `FormEngine` component [1].
The pages most relevant to rendering are:

- `field-types-and-renderings.mdx` — the table of `type` → adapter and `rendering` → control [2]
- `form-engine-implementations.mdx` — React vs Angular engine, and which package fills which role [3]
- `form-schema-reference.mdx` — the schema shape, including a starter obs question [4]
- Plus `expressions-validation-and-logic.mdx`, `advanced-form-capabilities.mdx`, `build-forms-with-o3-form-builder.mdx`, `convert-html-form-entry-forms.mdx`, `using-forms-in-applications.mdx` and `forms-troubleshooting.mdx` in the same directory.
A repository-level pointer also exists in `key-repositories.mdx`, which describes the React Form Engine as the successor to the Angular one [5].
## How obs rendering works in the library

**1. Two independent lookups.** The docs summarise this as "`type` selects a field-value adapter… `rendering` selects the input or display control" [6]. In code, the adapter is looked up by `field.type` in `formFieldAdapters` [7], which is built from `inbuiltFieldValueAdapters`, where `obs` and `obsGroup` both map to `ObsAdapter` [8]. The control is looked up by `questionOptions.rendering` in `inbuiltControls`, e.g. `text` → `TextField`, `radio` → `Radio`, `checkbox` → `MultiSelect` [9].

**2. Control resolution with a fallback.** `FormFieldRenderer` resolves the control through `getFieldControlWithFallback` [10]. That helper first checks for a missing concept and, unless the rendering is `file`, renders a disabled `text` control instead [11]; otherwise `getRegisteredControl` checks the in-memory cache, then built-in controls, then third-party registered controls [12].

**3. Loading existing obs into the form.** Before rendering, the encounter processor's `getInitialValues` asks each field's adapter for its initial value and stores it under the field id [13], triggered by `useInitialValues` [14]. For an obs field this is `ObsAdapter.getInitialValue`, which flattens the encounter's obs list and finds the obs belonging to that field [15]. Matching is done by `findObsByFormField`, which prefers the stored form-field path `` rfe-forms-${field.id} `` and falls back to matching by concept while excluding already-claimed obs uuids [16]. The raw obs is then reduced to a primitive value by `extractFieldValue`: checkbox renderings collect all value uuids, `toggle` compares against `ConceptTrue` [17], `date`/`datetime` renderings are parsed into date objects (a `timer` picker keeps only the clock time) [18], and everything else returns the value or its uuid [19].

**4. Rendering the input.** The control is wrapped in a react-hook-form `Controller`, so `setFieldValue` both updates the form value and runs `handleAfterChange` [20]. The same block conditionally renders the "unspecified" checkbox and the previous-value review, each guarded by `isUnspecifiedSupported` [21] and `PreviousValueReview` [22]. Controls that show a coded obs to the user ask the same adapter to translate the stored uuid into a label, via `getDisplayValue` [23], which is what `dropdown.component.tsx` and `multi-select.component.tsx` call [24].

**5. Turning the user's edit back into obs.** `handleAfterChange` first validates the value and then calls the adapter's `transformFieldValue` only if there are no validation errors [25]. `ObsAdapter.transformFieldValue` is the interesting part: it clears the stale pending submission [26], routes checkboxes to `handleMultiSelect` [27] and `file` renderings to `handleAttachments` [28], and otherwise decides among four outcomes:

| Situation | Result | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New value differs from a stored obs | `editObs` (keeps the uuid, updates value) | [29] |
| Unchanged value on a stored obs | `null` — deliberately nothing, to avoid a uuid-less duplicate | [30] |
| Stored obs cleared | `voidObs` marks it voided | [31] |
| Brand-new value | `constructObs` builds a fresh obs | [32] |

`constructObs` stamps every new obs with the namespace `rfe-forms` and the path `` rfe-forms-${field.id} `` [33] — the same path the read side matches on, which is how a form round-trips its own data. `handleMultiSelect` covers the three multi-select cases (clear all, partial change, all new) by computing which obs to void and which to create [34]. `hasPreviousObsValueChanged` guards the edit path and compares dates at the precision of the picker rather than the raw timestamp [35], with `formatDateByPickerType` handling the `timer` / `both` / `calendar` formats [36].

**Why it is built this way:** the schema's `type` and `rendering` are orthogonal [37], so a coded obs can be shown as `radio`, `select` or `content-switcher` without the submission logic changing, and third-party modules can register extra controls or adapters instead of patching the library [38]. The `assignedObsIds` list exists so that one obs is never bound to two fields, and it is cleared on teardown [39].

```mermaid
---
title: Obs field render, edit and submit path
---
flowchart TD
  Section["SectionRenderer looks up adapter by field.type"] --> Renderer["FormFieldRenderer"]
  Renderer --> Controls["getFieldControlWithFallback picks control by rendering"]
  Processor["getInitialValues asks adapter for value"] --> ObsAdapter["ObsAdapter.getInitialValue"]
  ObsAdapter --> Find["findObsByFormField by formFieldPath or concept"]
  ObsAdapter --> Extract["extractFieldValue reduces obs to primitive"]
  Extract --> Controller["Controller passes value to control"]
  Controller --> Change["setFieldValue then handleAfterChange"]
  Change --> Validate["validateFieldValue"]
  Validate --> Transform["ObsAdapter.transformFieldValue"]
  Transform --> Edit["editObs"]
  Transform --> Void["voidObs"]
  Transform --> Construct["constructObs"]
  Transform --> Skip["return null when unchanged"]
  Display["getDisplayValue maps uuid to label"] --> Controls
```

### What I could not verify
I read the documentation index and its `_meta.js` listing, but not every page in `forms-in-o3` (for example `expressions-validation-and-logic.mdx` and `advanced-form-capabilities.mdx`), so there may be further rendering detail there. I also did not read the individual control implementations beyond `ui-select-extended`, nor the `control-templates` mapping that backs renderings such as `drug` and `problem`.

code: This section is the canonical guide to the O3 Forms workflow shipped by the OpenMRS Reference Application. In that workflow, the O3 Form Builder creates and previews schemas with the React Form Engine, and the React Form Engine renders published O3 JSON forms at runtime. A form can also be converted from an existing HTML Form Entry form or rendered by a custom frontend module when an application needs a focused form workflow. O3 can surface configured HTML Form Entry forms through the patient ch

- `@openmrs/esm-form-builder-app` provides the Form Builder at `${openmrsSpaBase}/form-builder`. It previews forms with the React Form Engine and expects FHIR2 `>=1.2` and REST Web Services `>=2.2.0` on the backend.
- `@openmrs/esm-patient-forms-app` provides the patient chart form entry workspace. It renders configured HTML Form Entry forms in an iframe and renders O3 JSON forms through the `form-widget-slot`.
- `@openmrs/esm-form-engine-lib` provides the `FormEngine` component for custom rendering, submission handling, and embedded form views.

Start with [building forms with the O3 Form Builder](/docs/forms-in-o3/build-forms-with-o3-form-builder) when you are authoring a new O3 form. Use [converting HTML Form Entry forms](/docs/forms-in-o3/convert-html-form-entry-forms) when you are migrating existing HFE forms. Read [using forms in applications](/docs/forms-in-o3/using-forms-in-applications) when you need to launch the patient chart form workspace or render `FormEngine` directly.

If your distribution uses a form renderer other than the Reference Application default, read [Form engine implementations](/docs/forms-in-o3/form-engine-implementations) before choosing an authoring or testing workflow.

Only published O3 JSON forms are shown in the default React Form Engine workflow in the patient chart. Configured HTML Form Entry forms are handled separately by the patient forms app. Keep important schemas in version control or in a distribution repo, especially when working on demo servers that can be reset.
In the React Form Engine, `type` and `questionOptions.rendering` are independent contracts:
- `type` selects a field-value adapter, which reads existing data and creates submission data.
- `rendering` selects the input or display control.
The Form Builder exposes choices for authoring, but its dropdown is not a guarantee that a type/rendering combination has
the metadata or server support it needs. The builder preview renders through the React Form Engine.

For new implementations, we recommend the React Form Engine. It is included in the Reference Application and powers the O3 Form Builder preview, so forms use the same engine during authoring and at runtime. Existing implementations that depend on Angular forms or custom extensions can continue using the Angular integration while assessing migration. Test those forms and extensions against React before switching engines.
| Role | Default React workflow | Angular workflow |

| Form builder | [`@openmrs/esm-form-builder-app`](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-form-builder), which previews forms with the React Form Engine | No supported Angular preview in the O3 Form Builder |
| Reference Application status | Included by default | Not included by default |

Both integration modules register a renderer in `form-widget-slot`. A distribution should enable the integration that matches its Forms workflow, not both integrations as competing renderers for the same slot.
